questions.q: What are the four key functions of management?
questions.explain: These functions are carried out by managers at every level.
questions.evidence: This process is based in four key functional areas of the organization: planning, organizing, leading, and controlling.

questions.q: What is the difference between efficiency and effectiveness?
options: Efficiency uses the fewest resources to get work done; effectiveness produces the desired result
Efficiency is about people; effectiveness is about machines
questions.explain: Good managers need both.
questions.evidence: Efficiency is using the least possible amount of resources to get work done, whereas effectiveness is the ability to produce a desired result.

questions.q: What are the four basic types of planning?
questions.explain: They differ in time horizon and level of detail.
questions.evidence: There are four basic types of planning: strategic, tactical, operational, and contingency.

questions.q: In management, what is a role?
options: A job title on a business card
A set of behavioural expectations or activities a person is expected to perform
questions.explain: Managers play interpersonal, informational and decisional roles.
questions.evidence: A role is a set of behavioral expectations, or a set of activities that a person is expected to perform.

questions.q: What is leadership?
options: The process of guiding and motivating others toward the achievement of organisational goals
questions.explain: Leadership is the third key management function.
questions.evidence: is the process of guiding and motivating others toward the achievement of organizational goals.

questions.q: What is the ability to influence others to behave in a particular way called?
questions.explain: Leaders draw on different sources of power, from expertise to position.
questions.evidence: This ability to influence others to behave in a particular way is called power.

questions.q: In a crisis, what should managers always do?
options: Tell the truth about the situation and put the best people on the job to correct the problem
questions.explain: Honesty and fast, capable action minimise negative outcomes.
questions.evidence: Managers should always tell the truth about the situation and then put the best people on the job to correct the problem.

questions.q: How is a 'need' best defined in motivation theory?
options: Anything a person wants to buy
A reward given by a manager
The gap between what is and what is required
questions.explain: A want, by contrast, is the gap between what is and what is desired.
questions.evidence: A need is best defined as the gap between what is and what is required

questions.q: According to Maslow's hierarchy, what are the most basic human needs?
options: Physiological needs — food, shelter and clothing
questions.explain: Once a need is satisfied, a higher-level need becomes more motivating.
questions.evidence: the most basic human needs are physiological needs, that is, the needs for food, shelter, and clothing.

questions.q: In the workplace, what does 'equity' refer to?
options: Employees' perceived fairness of how they are treated and the rewards they earn
questions.explain: People compare their inputs and rewards with others'.
questions.evidence: in the workplace it refers to employees’ perceived fairness of the way they are treated and the rewards they earn.

questions.q: What is job rotation?
options: Shifting workers from one job to another — also called cross-training
questions.explain: It builds skills but raises training costs and briefly lowers productivity.
questions.evidence: Also called cross-training, job rotation is the shifting of workers from one job to another.

questions.q: When does a group become a team?
options: When it has more than ten members
When the common goals are clear and attention is paid to both interpersonal and task functions
questions.explain: A team charter and communication guidelines help.
questions.evidence: Groups become Teams if the common goals are clear and attention is paid to both interpersonal and task functions.

questions.q: What is planning, as a management function?
options: Deciding what must be done to reach objectives, when and how, and who will do it
Measuring results after the work is done
questions.explain: Planning is the first of the four management functions.
questions.evidence: planning is deciding what needs to be done to achieve organizational objectives, identifying when and how it will be done, and determining who should do it

questions.q: What is critical to successful strategic planning?
options: Focusing only on this week's tasks
Evaluating external factors such as economic, technological and social issues
questions.explain: Strategic plans are broad and long term.
questions.evidence: An evaluation of external environmental factors such as economic, technological, and social issues is critical to successful strategic planning.

questions.q: Planning to spend a few hours in the library this weekend is which kind of plan?
questions.explain: Planning to attend graduate school would be strategic.
questions.evidence: Some plans are much more specific and short term (more operational in nature), such as planning to spend a few hours in the library this weekend.

questions.q: How do autocratic leaders lead?
options: Directively, allowing very little input from subordinates
By putting every decision to a vote
questions.explain: Treated fairly, employees may still see them as decisive.
questions.evidence: Autocratic leaders are directive leaders, allowing for very little input from subordinates.

questions.q: What do consensual leaders require?
options: That all parties agree to the final decision after discussion
questions.explain: Consensual is one of the three types of participative leadership.
questions.evidence: Consensual leaders encourage discussion about issues and then require that all parties involved agree to the final decision.

questions.q: When can free-rein (laissez-faire) leadership frustrate employees?
options: When the leader gives too many orders
When it comes with unclear expectations and no feedback
questions.explain: Free rein works best with clear expectations and capable staff.
questions.evidence: If free-rein leadership is accompanied by unclear expectations and lack of feedback from the manager, the experience can be frustrating for an employee.

questions.q: Which are four important trends in management today, according to the chapter?
options: Longer meetings, more paperwork, fewer staff and less travel
Lower pay, fewer holidays, more rules and less training
Crisis management, outside directors, information technology and global skills
questions.explain: Each trend changes what managers need to know.
questions.evidence: Four important trends in management today are crisis management, outside directors, the growing use of information technology, and the increasing need for global management skills.

questions.q: What should managers do after a crisis is resolved?
options: Forget it as quickly as possible
Learn from the experience to avoid the same problem in future
questions.explain: Telling the truth and putting the best people on the problem also matter.
questions.evidence: managers must learn from the experience to avoid the same problem in the future

questions.q: According to Maslow, what happens once a need is satisfied?
options: It matters less, and a higher-level need becomes more motivating
questions.explain: This is why motivation changes as people's situations change.
questions.evidence: Once a need is satisfied, its importance to the individual diminishes, and a higher-level need is more likely to motivate the person.

questions.q: What are esteem needs in Maslow's hierarchy?
options: Needs for others' respect and a sense of accomplishment
questions.explain: They sit at the fourth level of the hierarchy.
questions.evidence: esteem needs, which are needs for the respect of others and for a sense of accomplishment and achievement

questions.q: What view of human nature underlies McGregor's Theory X?
options: An optimistic one — people seek responsibility
A neutral one — people only want money
A pessimistic one — the average person dislikes work and avoids it
A view that work is a form of play
questions.explain: Theory Y takes the opposite, optimistic view.
questions.evidence: The Theory X management style is based on a pessimistic view of human nature

questions.q: What does expectancy theory focus on?
options: The link between motivation and behaviour
questions.explain: It is one of the best-supported theories of motivation.
questions.evidence: expectancy theory, which focuses on the link between motivation and behavior

questions.q: Why is feedback so important in goal-setting theory?
options: It shows the gap between actual performance and the goal
It replaces the need for goals
It is only needed after failure
questions.explain: Specific, challenging goals plus feedback improve performance.
questions.evidence: Feedback is particularly important because it helps the individual identify the gap between the real (the actual performance) and the ideal (the desired outcome defined by the goal).

questions.q: What is job enlargement?
options: Increasing the number and variety of tasks a person performs
questions.explain: It is a horizontal expansion of the job.
questions.evidence: The horizontal expansion of a job, increasing the number and variety of tasks that a person performs, is called job enlargement.

questions.q: What is a potential drawback of job enlargement?
options: Employees may feel they work harder with no extra responsibility or pay
questions.explain: Job enrichment, which adds responsibility, can avoid this.
questions.evidence: employees may perceive that they are being asked to work harder and do more with no change in their level of responsibility or compensation

questions.q: What are the drawbacks of job rotation?
options: Higher training costs and lower productivity while people get up to speed
It cannot cover for absent staff
questions.explain: Its benefits include flexibility and cover for absences.
questions.evidence: Drawbacks of job rotation include an increase in training costs and decreased productivity

questions.q: Why train employees properly in new technologies?
options: They become more productive and less resistant to job change
It lets the company cut all salaries
It removes the need for managers
questions.explain: Training builds confidence with new tools.
questions.evidence: Employees who are properly trained in new technologies are more productive and less resistant to job change.

questions.q: Why can an employee stock ownership plan (ESOP) be an attractive exit strategy?
options: It sells the company to a competitor
Employees paid in stock can gradually become the company's owners
questions.explain: It offers owners a smooth transition.
questions.evidence: Because ESOP employees are compensated with stock, over time they can become the owners of the company, an attractive exit strategy for current owners seeking a smooth transition.

questions.q: Which tool do some companies use to help employees achieve work-life balance?
questions.explain: Less stressed employees focus better and are more productive.
questions.evidence: One tool companies are using to help their employees achieve work-life balance is the sabbatical.

questions.q: What is human resource management?
options: Hiring, developing, motivating and evaluating employees to achieve goals
questions.explain: HR systems aim to make employees a source of competitive advantage.
questions.evidence: Human resource (HR) management is the process of hiring, developing, motivating, and evaluating employees to achieve organizational goals.

questions.q: Why is the human resource management process sequential?
options: Employees can't be trained and paid until they are selected and placed
Laws require a fixed order of paperwork
questions.explain: Planning and job design come before recruitment and selection.
questions.evidence: The process is sequential because employees can’t be trained and paid until selected and placed in jobs

questions.q: Which skills must team members have and use?
options: Leadership, decision-making, trust-building, communication and conflict management
questions.explain: Groups become teams when goals are clear and both task and people matter.
questions.evidence: the needed leadership, decision-making, trust-building, communication, and conflict-management skills

questions.q: What should each team set up for good communication?
options: A single rule written by management
Its own communication guidelines and a team charter
A weekly report to HR only
questions.explain: Members negotiate what matters most for clear communication.
questions.evidence: Each Team must set up their own guidelines for good communication and a Team Charter.

questions.q: What kind of team does building and running a digital service need?
options: A multidisciplinary team with a range of skills
questions.explain: The team must also work with others across the organisation.
questions.evidence: your delivery team needs to be multidisciplinary and have a range of skills

questions.q: What is a digital service usually part of?
options: A wider change to how an organisation operates
questions.explain: For example, contact-centre changes when a new policy starts.
questions.evidence: A digital service is usually part of a wider change to how an organisation operates

questions.q: Does a service team need the same skills in every development phase?
options: No — different phases need different skills
questions.explain: Plan the resources each phase requires, including for secure practices.
questions.evidence: need different skills during the different development phases
